title: Mapping the prefilter db raised seeding misc time and peak RSS
body:
Commit `41781f9` changed `PrefilterDb` in `mmseqs.rs` to map each split file of an mmseqs prefilter or align db with `libsail::source::MmapSource`, in place of opening the file for every record. On 20,795 Pfam profiles against 2,455,940 targets at `-t 8`, with a 32 GB prefilter db, two numbers got worse while decide, slice and merge improved:

| measure | `012b26c` | `41781f9` |
|---|---|---|
| seeding `[misc.]` | 0.23 s | 0.74 s |
| peak RSS, from `/usr/bin/time -v` | 4.8 GB | 7.4 GB |

Seeding `[misc.]` holds `PrefilterDb::from_path` on the prefilter db. Its validation reads the byte after every record, so through the map it touches one page per record across the 32 GB. The run reported 982 major page faults, so some of those pages came from disk. Mapped pages count toward RSS once touched. They are clean, and the kernel can drop them, but the number a user sees rose by 2.6 GB. Neither cause has been measured on its own; both are readings of the numbers above.

## Proposal

Measure each cost on its own before changing anything:

- time `PrefilterDb::from_path` on the prefilter db alone, with a warm and a cold page cache
- record RSS over the seeding stage, to see which of slice, decide and merge touches the most pages

## Open

- Whether `from_path` needs to check every null byte at all, or whether a check on read would do.
- Whether `madvise` on the map changes either cost.
close_reason: The `[misc.]` time came from the null-byte check in `PrefilterDb::from_path`, which faulted in one page per record: 6.9 s cold, 0.03 s warm, 1.3 GB left resident. `c1cc1c0` moves the check to the read. The RSS rise is mapped file pages, not allocation; that finding moved to nail-2b1402, which decides whether `PrefilterDb` keeps its map.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text:
Measured at `1e1bac3` with a copy of `PrefilterDb` in `tmp-claude/2026-10-15-prefilter-map`. The input was the 32 GB prefilter db of the full run: 20,795 records over 8 split files, in `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-serial-overhead/nail-tmp/prefilter-db`. For a cold cache, `evict.py` in the same directory drops the files' pages with `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)`. The box has 60 GB of RAM.

## `from_path`

| step | cold | warm |
|---|---|---|
| read the index | 0.002 s | 0.002 s |
| map the 8 files | 0.000 s | 0.000 s |
| null-byte check | 6.87 s, 10,012 major faults | 0.028 s |

The check reads one byte per record, yet it leaves 1,298 MB of the file resident (`RssFile`), because each page fault maps the 64 KB around its address. The full run had 982 major faults and 0.74 s in seeding `[misc.]`, which fits a check whose pages were mostly still cached after mmseqs wrote them. On a box whose page cache cannot hold the db, the check would approach the cold 6.9 s.

## Slicing

The probe repeats the slice loop of `seed_progressive` with `--prog-n 200` and doubling. It keeps every query active, so it reads more than a real run, which stops querying records once decide terminates them.

| after | sliced this iteration | `RssFile` | `RssAnon` |
|---|---|---|---|
| null check | | 1,298 MB | 0 MB |
| iteration 4 | 960 MB | 3,074 MB | 1 MB |
| iteration 7 | 7,183 MB | 15,189 MB | 1 MB |
| iteration 10 | 2,305 MB | 31,599 MB | 1 MB |

All the growth is file pages, which are clean and which the kernel can drop. `RssAnon` stays at 1 MB. Peak RSS (`VmHWM`) counts file pages, so the 4.8 GB to 7.4 GB rise in the full run is the mapped prefilter db, not memory nail allocated. Before `41781f9`, nail read the same bytes into the page cache with `read`, which does not count toward the process's RSS.
